title: Add the blog content system and pages
context: Replace the scaffolded blog routes with a static, repository-authored MDX collection and Figma-aligned listing and article experiences. The blog listing follows Figma file 0J2JF0nYrI8EJrttdHNes4 node 652:141, and the article follows node 652:448. The initial collection uses the three existing homepage insights, lists every post without pagination, and models tutorials as tagged blog posts. `/blog` and `/tutorial` may share low-level post-card/grid primitives, but they must remain separate route compositions so the tutorial experience can diverge later. Long-form content introduces a reusable `responsive-text` wrapper sized from a responsive root and constrained with character-based width; migrating the existing legal pages to it is explicitly deferred. Because no tutorial assignment was supplied, this plan uses `margin-top-for-the-win` as the initial tutorial so the filtered route has a real, testable result.

tasks.title: Create the typed MDX post collection
acceptance_criteria: Next.js 16 is configured for local MDX using the documented App Router integration, including the required MDX components entry point, while preserving static server rendering and adding no client-side content loader.

A typed canonical post registry exposes slug, title, description, publication date, display sequence, and tags/category data, rejects invalid duplicate slugs or unsupported metadata at build/type-check time, and returns posts newest-first.

Repository-authored MDX files exist for `margin-top-for-the-win`, `working-on-old-hardware`, and `hello-world`, using the titles, summaries, dates, and 003/002/001 sequence already shown on the homepage and in Figma rather than lorem ipsum listing data.

Tutorial membership is expressed in post metadata instead of a separate content collection, with `margin-top-for-the-win` initially tagged as a tutorial and reusable selectors exposing all posts or tutorial-only posts.

The homepage insight cards read their title, description, date label, slug, and href from the canonical post metadata while keeping homepage-only visibility behavior in the homepage presentation layer.
Adding another post has one documented content workflow and does not require editing the blog listing or tutorial page components.

tasks.title: Build the blog and tutorial listing routes
acceptance_criteria: `/blog` renders a `Latest Insights` heading and every canonical post exactly once in newest-first order, with no pagination controls or repeated Figma filler cards.
`/tutorial` renders a `Tutorials` heading and only posts whose canonical metadata includes the tutorial classification; non-tutorial posts are absent.
The two routes are separate page compositions and can diverge independently, while sharing focused post-card and post-grid primitives rather than a single title-switched page template.

Cards reuse the existing linked-panel interaction and match Figma node 652:141 for surface, asymmetric radius, metadata, title, description, read-more affordance, spacing, and desktop three-column composition.
The post grid is mobile-first with one column below 48rem, two columns from 48rem to below 62rem, and three columns at 62rem and above, using the repository's exact native range-query conventions.
Every card is a semantic, keyboard-accessible single-destination article link with a descriptive accessible name, visible focus treatment, and a working `/blog/[slug]` destination.
Both listings retain the shared site header, main landmark/skip-link target, noise background, and footer, and introduce no unnecessary client JavaScript.

tasks.title: Address feedback on task 2: Unify insight card typography and row heights
acceptance_criteria: Blog and tutorial card metadata, title, description, and read-more typography use the same CSS values as the homepage insight cards, so the canonical post previews retain one consistent type scale across routes.

At every multi-column breakpoint, cards in the same blog, tutorial, and homepage insight-grid row have equal visible surface heights; each linked-panel surface fills its grid row without changing single-column behavior or link semantics.

Focused browser coverage verifies the shared typography values and equal-height behavior for the homepage and blog listing at a multi-column viewport, while preserving the existing responsive grid and accessibility coverage.
`npm run verify` passes with lint, strict TypeScript, production static generation, and Playwright coverage.

tasks.title: Address feedback on task 3: Remove insight panel minimum heights
acceptance_criteria: Blog, tutorial, and homepage insight panels have no explicit `min-height`; their height is determined solely by content and the equal-height grid-row stretch behavior.
At multi-column breakpoints, cards in the same row still have equal visible surface heights, while single-column cards do not reserve unnecessary vertical space.
Focused browser coverage verifies the absence of an explicit panel minimum height and preserves the existing typography, equal-height, responsive-grid, and accessible-link assertions.
`npm run verify` passes with lint, strict TypeScript, production static generation, and Playwright coverage.

tasks.title: Render static responsive blog posts
acceptance_criteria: Each canonical slug renders its matching MDX body at `/blog/[slug]`, all known slugs are prerendered with `generateStaticParams`, unknown slugs return 404, and no post requires runtime data fetching.

Each post supplies route metadata derived from the canonical title and description and renders one semantic article with a single page-level heading followed by correctly nested MDX headings and prose.

The article composition matches Figma node 652:448 at the 1280px reference viewport, including the shared header/footer, top and bottom spacing, display headline, Source Serif body copy, and restrained background treatment.

The entire article typography region is wrapped by the reusable literal `responsive-text` class; its root evaluates to 3.75vw at mobile reference widths and 1.352vw at the 1280px desktop reference, with bounded intermediate scaling that does not create a breakpoint jump or unreadable text.
Typography inside `responsive-text` uses em-relative sizes and spacing derived from that root rather than independent viewport, px, or rem font sizes.
The prose measure is expressed with a ch-based width, remains within page gutters, and is visually calibrated to approximately 776px of content width at a 1280px viewport.
The responsive text primitive is architecture-neutral and reusable by future long-form routes, but the privacy policy and terms pages are not migrated in this feature.

Post prose, headings, lists, links, inline code, code blocks, blockquotes, and images have accessible, overflow-safe default treatments, including visible link focus and horizontal containment for long technical content.

tasks.title: Address feedback on task 5: Move post metadata into validated frontmatter
acceptance_criteria: Every `src/content/blog/*.mdx` post owns validated YAML frontmatter with required `title`, `description`, quoted `publishedAt` in `YYYY-MM-DD` format, and `tags` fields; an optional `socialImage` object is accepted only when it supplies both a public-root `src` and non-empty `alt` text.

The post loader discovers MDX files at build time, derives each slug from its lowercase kebab-case filename, rejects malformed filenames or metadata with actionable errors, and requires no hand-maintained metadata array or content import map.
Tags are unique normalized kebab-case strings, `tutorial` continues to determine tutorial membership, and adding a new valid tag does not require editing a central allowlist.

Display sequence is derived rather than authored: posts are numbered chronologically with the oldest as `001`; equal publication dates use filename ascending as the deterministic tie-breaker, while listings remain newest-date-first with filename ascending for equal dates.

All three existing posts are migrated without changing their canonical titles, descriptions, dates, tutorial membership, generated routes, display labels, or article prose; body-level duplicate `h1` headings are removed so the article shell remains the sole page-level heading.

Article bodies use Next.js 16's documented static dynamic-MDX-import pattern, all discovered slugs remain covered by `generateStaticParams`, unknown slugs remain 404s, and no runtime content fetching or client-side content loader is introduced.

`src/content/blog/README.md` documents the one-file authoring workflow and includes a copy/paste frontmatter template, filename and date rules, description guidance, tutorial tagging, optional custom social-image fields, automatic ordering/numbering behavior, and expected validation failures.
Focused tests cover successful discovery and rendering plus invalid frontmatter, filename, date, tag, duplicate-tag, partial-social-image, automatic-sequence, and same-day tie-break behavior.

tasks.title: Add origin-aware article navigation
acceptance_criteria: A small client-side provider at the marketing route-group boundary tracks a `blog` or `tutorial` article origin during client navigation without moving article content, metadata loading, or route generation to the client.
Blog and homepage post cards set Blog as the origin, tutorial cards set Tutorials as the origin, and all default card destinations remain clean `/blog/[slug]` URLs without query parameters.

A visible keyboard-accessible link appears above every article header and resolves to `< Back to Blog` at `/blog` by default or `< Back to Tutorials` at `/tutorial` when the article was opened from the tutorial listing.
The resolved article origin also controls desktop and mobile primary-navigation highlighting so exactly one of Blog or Tutorials is active on a post route.

An explicit `?from=tutorial` query hint selects the tutorial back link and navigation state for direct or shareable URLs; invalid query values are ignored, and the canonical article URL never includes the origin query.
Direct article traffic, new sessions, and reloads without a valid query hint default to Blog, while session-only origin state may intentionally reset on refresh.

Browser coverage verifies Blog, Tutorials, and homepage entry paths; direct and refreshed traffic; query-assisted direct links; back-link destinations; desktop and mobile active states; keyboard activation; and unchanged static article rendering.

tasks.title: Add blog SEO and social sharing metadata
acceptance_criteria: The root metadata uses `https://brent.walbolt.com` as `metadataBase` and identifies Brent Walbolt as the site author, creator, and publisher.

Every post derives its title, description, canonical `/blog/[slug]` URL, keywords, Open Graph article fields, publication date, author, tags, and Twitter `summary_large_image` fields from validated post data.

A shared 1200 by 630 branded social image using the existing dark navy visual language, logo, and portfolio tagline is the default for all posts; a valid frontmatter `socialImage` overrides the shared image and alt text for both Open Graph and Twitter.
Every post emits valid `BlogPosting` JSON-LD containing its canonical URL, headline, description, publication date, author, tags, and resolved social image.
The `/blog` and `/tutorial` listings expose descriptive titles, descriptions, and canonical URLs, and origin hints such as `?from=tutorial` never produce duplicate canonical URLs.

Static `robots.ts` and `sitemap.ts` outputs allow indexing, reference the canonical sitemap URL, and include the homepage, primary static routes, blog/tutorial listings, and every discovered post with its publication date.

Automated coverage inspects rendered canonical, Open Graph, Twitter, and JSON-LD output; shared and custom image selection; canonical query exclusion; robots and sitemap responses; and preservation of unknown-post 404 behavior.

tasks.title: Document and verify the complete blog flow
acceptance_criteria: Browser coverage verifies all three frontmatter-derived blog cards and routes, newest-first and same-day ordering, automatic display sequences, the tutorial-only filter, an unknown-slug 404, card and back-link keyboard navigation, semantic headings, and the absence of pagination.

Browser coverage verifies clean and query-assisted article-origin navigation, Blog-versus-Tutorials back links and active navigation states, canonical URLs, Open Graph/Twitter metadata, JSON-LD, sitemap coverage, and shared/custom social-image behavior.

Responsive browser coverage exercises 390, 479, 480, 767, 768, 991, 992, 1279, and 1280px widths without horizontal page overflow and asserts the listing column transitions, responsive-text root sizing, approximately 776px desktop prose measure, and usable origin-aware controls.
Visual comparison against Figma nodes 652:141 and 652:448 confirms the requested desktop compositions and records any deliberate mobile or back-link adaptations based on the repository design system.

ARCHITECTURE.md and DESIGN.md document the filesystem/frontmatter content pipeline, filename-derived slugs, date-derived sequences, tutorial classification, separate listing-route ownership, session/query article origin, canonical/social metadata behavior, responsive-text/ch measure convention, and deferred legal-page migration.

`npm run verify` passes with lint, strict TypeScript, production build/static generation, and Playwright coverage, with no runtime post fetching, unnecessary client content loading, accessibility regressions, or loss of static generation.
